questions.q: When does Li-Ion beat LiPo on board?
options: With T/W above 5 and short flights
questions.explain: Average current ≤ 1–2C and a long flight: Li-Ion gives more Wh/kg but is limited in current.

questions.q: How do you calculate the resistance of a 6S4P pack of 25 mΩ cells?
questions.explain: In series it adds up (×S), in parallel it divides (÷P).

questions.q: Why must you not solder to 18650/21700 cells?
questions.explain: Overheating the terminal damages the separator and the protection; spot welding heats only the spot, for milliseconds.

questions.q: What's wrong with nickel-plated steel strip?
questions.explain: Pure nickel is the standard for current paths.

questions.q: Why is a classic BMS dangerous in flight?
options: A cutoff in the air = a crash
It's heavy and interferes with the GPS antenna
questions.explain: For flying packs, voltage protection is done by the flight controller, not the BMS.

questions.q: How do you measure the real capacity of a pack?
options: By a discharge with current integration
By the resting voltage an hour after charging
questions.explain: Discharge under load down to 3.0 V/cell while integrating current: only ∫I·dt gives the real delivered capacity.

questions.q: What does an IR difference between groups > 30% mean?
questions.explain: A bad weld or cell: the high-R group sags first and heats up.

questions.q: The resistance of a pack of cells with resistance R:
questions.explain: Resistances add up in series and divide in parallel: R·S/P.
